sections.heading: The Perfect Fifth Interval
sections.body: The perfect fifth is a consonant interval that helps us organize and clearly see many structures that exist in music. Based on the harmonic series that arises from the natural vibration of a string, we choose it because, taking it as a unit of measure and applying it consecutively, it is an interval that lets us traverse the 12 pitch classes used in Western music (the full chromatic set of sounds).

sections.heading: The tonic is grade 1
sections.body: Whichever mode column you mark as grade 1 is the tonic — the home of the scale you are reading. By default that is Ionian, which is just the major scale under its older name. Tap another mode name and the degree numbers rotate so that column becomes 1.

sections.heading: Ionian is Major, Aeolian is Minor
sections.body: Ionian and Aeolian are the everyday Major and Minor scales. The board labels them that way so you can find them without memorising Greek names first. Choosing Aeolian as grade 1 is how you read a natural minor key on the same strip.
